program_name: Ohio State Nutrition (OSUN) Interdisciplinary PhD in Nutrition
department_or_school: OSU Nutrition interdisciplinary graduate program (faculty across Human Sciences, Food Science, Animal Sciences, Medicine, Nursing, etc.)
spring_2027_deadline: Not verified (no spring entry term found on OSUN pages)
fall_2027_deadline: Preferred deadline December 1 (for Graduate School Fellowship and programmatic funding consideration) per OSUN Graduate Program Handbook; 2027-cycle date not separately posted - confirm on gpadmissions program page prog=0156
funding_deadline_note: Handbook: December 1 is the preferred application deadline if applying for Graduate School Fellowship and Programmatic funding. Financial aid page: review starts in December; most decisions by end of March.
ielts_subscore_note: Graduate School minimum (IELTS Academic or IELTS Online); IELTS One Skill Retake not accepted. CONFLICT: an OIA exchange-student page and a Sept 2025 Anthropology department guide list 7.0, but the official admissions page and Graduate School Handbook say 6.5.
toefl_min: 79 iBT (4.0 on updated TOEFL from Jan 2026); Duolingo 120
funding_summary: OSUN future-students page: all students receive financial support for the duration of their Ph.D. studies through fellowships and/or associateships from the University, Program and/or advisor, and department. Admitted students are awarded a first-year graduate research associateship (GRA) on a competitive basis; some receive University Fellowships. Handbook: programmatic support generally does not exceed one year, after which support comes through the dissertation advisor; 50%+ fellowship/GRA/GTA includes full tuition and fee authorization and a modest stipend.
notes: Admissions page: GRE no longer required (encouraged if it strengthens the application); minimum 3.30 cumulative GPA; master's preferred but exceptional bachelor's applicants with research experience may be admitted directly to the PhD. Applicants are encouraged to enter with a commitment from an OSUN faculty member to serve as mentor. Handbook: requests for OSUN to pay the international application fee are not normally approved.

program_name: Human Nutrition MS - Nutrition Research Specialization
department_or_school: Department of Human Sciences, College of Education and Human Ecology
spring_2027_deadline: Not verified - a 2020 MS handbook says admission can start Autumn or Spring, but the current Research Specialization page lists only the autumn deadline
fall_2027_deadline: December 1 (for highest priority funding consideration), then ongoing through summer until cohort filled; applications open September 1 (program page)
ielts_subscore_note: 6.5 is the OSU Graduate School minimum. CAUTION: the Oct 2020 Human Nutrition MS Graduate Studies Handbook lists IELTS 8.0 / TOEFL iBT 100 as program levels - possibly outdated; confirm with the program office before applying.
toefl_min: 79 iBT (Graduate School); 2020 program handbook listed 100 iBT
funding_summary: 2020 handbook: graduate research associateships and teaching associateships at 50% time or more include full tuition and fee coverage plus a monthly stipend; appointment decisions are made in the spring. No guarantee of funding stated.
notes: Biochemistry is a required prerequisite. Applicants should name a potential faculty advisor of interest (department checklist). Checklist lists HUMNTR-MS: No GRE.
